test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 19 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A cistern has two inlet pipes, A and B, and one outlet pipe, C. Pipe A can fill the cistern alone in 15 hours, pipe B in 18 hours, and pipe C can empty it in 27 hours. For the first 5 hours, pipes A and B are opened together. Then, for the next 12 hours, pipes B and C are opened together. After that, only pipe B works. How long will pipe B alone take to fill the remaining part of the cistern?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity = LCM of 15, 18, 27 = 270 units.

Efficiency: A = +18, B = +15, C = −10.

Work by (A + B) in 5 hrs = (18 + 15) × 5 = 165 units.

Work by (B + C) in 12 hrs = (15 − 10) × 12 = 60 units.

Remaining work = 270 − (165 + 60) = 45 units.

Time taken by B alone = 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the cistern = 15 hours

Time taken by Pipe B to fill the cistern = 18 hours

Time taken by Pipe C to empty the cistern = 27 hours

**Concept Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual times taken by the pipes.

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

For an emptying pipe, the efficiency is taken as negative.

 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Pipe A (+)

 Pipe B (+)
 18

 Pipe C (−)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined efficiency of Pipes A and B = 18 + 15 = 33 units/hr

⇒ Work done by A and B in the first 5 hours = 33 × 5 = 165 units

⇒ Combined efficiency of Pipes B and C = 15 + (−10) = 5 units/hr

⇒ Work done by B and C in the next 12 hours = 5 × 12 = 60 units

⇒ Total work done so far = 165 + 60 = 225 units

⇒ Remaining work to be done = 270 − 225 = 45 units

⇒ Time taken by Pipe B alone to finish the remaining work = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time taken = 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet vs Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank (positive efficiency +), whereas an outlet pipe empties it (negative efficiency −). The net rate is the algebraic sum of their individual rates.

Work and Wages

Wages are strictly distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual, not simply by their daily efficiency unless they work for the exact same number of days.

Alternate Working Hours

When pipes operate alternately, calculate the net work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 hours). Multiply the cycle to reach as close to total work without exceeding it, then manually add remaining work.
